title: Call for residency hosts 2026-2027
content:
The call for residency hosts provides financial support to legal entities wishing to host artists and cultural professionals for one residency project.

This call has two phases:

Submission of the application describing the residency project, together with the required supporting documents about the legal entity.

If selected in phase 1, applicants can proceed to choose the artists and cultural professionals who will be their residents. And then complete the second and final part of the application.

Legal entities that:

  • are registered and based in one of the Creative Europe countries, including the overseas countries and territories and outermost regions
  • have the capacity to host the proposed residency project with artists and cultural professionals from other Creative Europe countries
  • regardless of being a newly or well-established entity, applicants must be active in one of the eligible sectors: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts

    • The residency grant offers financial support to the host and each resident:

    €50 per day, per resident.

title: Culture Moves Europe: new call for residency hosts 2026-2027 open
content:
The call provides grants to organisations and individual artists from Creative Europe countries that wish to host international artists and cultural professionals for a residency project. Hosts can invite up to five residents and are expected to provide an appropriate environment, accommodation, workspace and artistic guidance through at least one mentor.

Residency projects should pursue at least two of five objectives:

  • explore
  • create
  • learn
  • connect
  • transform

    • The call is open to projects in the fields of

  • architecture
  • cultural heritage
  • design and fashion design
  • literature
  • music
  • performing arts
  • visual arts

    • Whether you are a non-profit organisation, cultural centre, museum, foundation, company, NGO or self-employed artist, you can apply to become a Culture Moves Europe residency host.

    The call is open until 18 January 2027.

    The call provides financial support to organisations and individual artists that want to host artists and cultural professionals for a residency project. Apply until 18 January 2027.

  • Find out more about the details of the call and how to apply for a residency

title: Culture Moves Europe: new call for individual mobility 2026–2027 open
content:
With a budget of €25 million, Culture Moves Europe supports around 7 000 artists, cultural professionals and host organisations between 2025 and 2028. The mobility action is funded by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union and is implemented by the Goethe-Institut.

Culture Moves Europe helps participants to:

  • develop international projects and partnerships
  • access new professional opportunities
  • strengthen skills through learning and exchange
  • increase the visibility of their work internationally
  • connect with diverse communities, peers and organisations

    • The call for individual mobility is open to both artists and cultural professionals from Creative Europe participating countries.

    Professionals active in the fields of

  • architecture
  • cultural heritage
  • design and fashion design
  • literature
  • music
  • performing arts
  • visual arts

    • may apply for the call.

    We encourage applications from both emerging and established professionals, including those seeking to internationalise their practice, explore new collaborations or reach new audiences across Europe and beyond.

    The Culture Moves Europe calls operate on a rolling basis, with evaluation periods at the end of every month during the application period:

title: Call for individual mobility 2026-2027
content:
Artists and cultural professionals, who are:

  • legally residing in one of the Creative Europe countries, including the overseas countries and territories and outermost regions
  • 18 years of age or older
  • active in one of the following sectors: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts; No specific level of experience is required

    • The call for individual mobility allows applications from individuals and groups of up to 5 people.

    €85 per day of project implementation.

  • €400 for travel distances under 5.000 km
  • €800 travel distance from 5.000 km

    • The travel distance is calculated automatically in the application form, based on a one-way straight line. The European Commission distance calculator may nevertheless be used for indicative estimates.

    The grant offers additional funding, if applicable:

  • green mobility top-up: €400
  • overseas countries and territories / Outermost regions top-up: €175
  • family top-up: €200 per child under 18 years old
  • visa top-up: €120
  • €30 per day of project implementation
  • either the actual cost or a fixed allowance for personal assistance or sign language interpretation, depending on the assistant’s professional status

title: Europe grows its network of experts in cultural heritage risk preparedness
content:
24 heritage professionals began their training in cultural heritage risk preparedness in June 2026 as part of a second group of specialists coming from 19 countries participating in the Creative Europe programme.

The training provided by the READY project involved two weeks of online learning followed by ten days of in-person training in Bucharest this September.

The new cohort joins the 24 professionals trained during the project's first year, forming a growing network dedicated to heritage risk management. In doing so, they have also built the knowledge and partnerships needed to protect heritage sites and associated living traditions from complex and cascading risks.

The training strengthens the ability of heritage professionals to safeguard immovable heritage and living traditions amid growing disaster risks, climate extremes and conflict. The participants developed practical skills and tools to assess and reduce disaster risk, improve emergency preparedness, coordinate cultural heritage first aid, and support early recovery.

title: Victoria will be the European Capital of Culture 2031 in Malta
content:
On 23 September 2026, the chairperson of the European Capitals of Culture expert panel announced Victoria as the recommended city for the European Capital of Culture 2031 title in Malta. The recommendation followed an assessment of the city’s application by the panel of independent experts.

After Valetta in 2018, Victoria will be the second Maltese city to hold this prestigious title.

After being the only city shortlisted, Victoria has been recommended by the panel of independent experts to become the 2031 European Capital of Culture in Malta.

In a world increasingly shaped by fragmentation and disconnection, Victoria seeks to turn its island condition into a source of connection. 
Through the theme “an Island of Islands”, Victoria 2031 explores the relationships between people, communities, places and Europe, seeing difference not as a source of isolation but as an opportunity for encounter, exchange and mutual enrichment. Slowness, care and courage provide the values for imagining more connected and collaborative futures.
